description: Haemul Pajeon is a beloved Korean savory pancake, packed with a delightful medley of fresh seafood and vibrant green onions. Its crispy edges and tender, flavorful interior make it an irresistible dish, perfect as an appetizer or a light meal. This recipe guides you to create an authentic and delicious version right in your own kitchen.

ingredients.notes: cleaned and cut into bite-sized pieces

instructions.title: Prepare the Dipping Sauce
instructions.text: Combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, toasted sesame seeds, and minced garlic in a small bowl. Stir well and set aside. This can be made in advance.

instructions.title: Make the Batter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, rice flour, cornstarch, salt, and egg. Gradually add the cold water, whisking until a smooth batter forms. Do not overmix; a few small lumps are acceptable.

instructions.title: Prepare Seafood and Vegetables
instructions.text: Ensure your seafood is thoroughly cleaned, drained, and cut into bite-sized pieces. Pat dry with paper towels to remove excess moisture. Cut green onions into 3-4 inch lengths. Thinly slice the small onion and red chili, if using.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the prepared seafood, green onions, and sliced onion to the batter. Gently fold everything together until the seafood and vegetables are evenly coated with the batter. Be careful not to break up the green onions too much.

instructions.title: Pan-Fry the Pancake
instructions.text: Heat a large non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil, ensuring it coats the bottom of the pan. Pour about 1/4 to 1/3 of the batter mixture into the hot pan, spreading it evenly to form a round pancake. Arrange some additional green onion pieces and seafood on top if desired for presentation.

instructions.title: Cook Until Golden and Crispy
instructions.text: Cook for 5-7 minutes on one side, or until the bottom is golden brown and crispy. Drizzle a little more oil around the edges, then carefully flip the pancake. Cook for another 5-7 minutes on the second side until golden brown and cooked through. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more oil as needed for each pancake.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Transfer the cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board and slice into wedges. Serve hot with the prepared dipping sauce. Enjoy this savory and crispy Korean seafood pancake as an appetizer or a delightful main dish.

tips: For the crispiest Pajeon, use very cold water for the batter and add a tablespoon or two of cooking oil to the batter itself.
Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches to ensure even cooking and crispiness. A hot pan and sufficient oil are key.
Serve immediately for the best texture. Leftovers can be reheated in a dry skillet or toaster oven to regain some crispiness.
article:
Dive into the heart of Korean comfort food with Haemul Pajeon, a savory seafood pancake that’s as delightful to make as it is to eat. This iconic dish, celebrated for its crispy edges, chewy interior, and abundant fresh ingredients, offers a perfect blend of textures and flavors. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a culinary novice, mastering Haemul Pajeon is a rewarding experience that brings a taste of Korea right to your kitchen. Get ready to explore everything about this beloved pancake, from its origins and essential ingredients to step-by-step cooking instructions and tips for achieving that perfect golden crisp.

## What is Haemul Pajeon?

Haemul Pajeon is a quintessential Korean savory pancake, where "haemul" means seafood and "pajeon" refers to a scallion pancake. Unlike the sweet, fluffy pancakes many are familiar with, pajeon is a robust, savory affair, typically pan-fried to a golden crisp. What sets Haemul Pajeon apart is its generous inclusion of various fresh seafood – often shrimp, squid, mussels, and oysters – intertwined with vibrant green onions and a light, flavorful batter. This combination results in a dish that is wonderfully chewy, subtly sweet from the seafood, and refreshingly aromatic from the scallions. Historically, pajeon has been a popular snack or appetizer, often enjoyed with makgeolli (Korean rice wine) on rainy days, a tradition believed to have stemmed from the sizzling sound of the pancake mimicking the sound of rain. Its appeal lies in its versatility and the comforting warmth it provides, making it a staple in Korean households and restaurants worldwide.

## Ingredients for Haemul Pajeon

Crafting the perfect Haemul Pajeon starts with fresh, high-quality ingredients. Here’s what you’ll typically need:

For the Batter:
*   1 cup Korean pancake mix (buchim garu) or a mix of all-purpose flour and rice flour
*   1 cup cold water or anchovy broth (for deeper flavor)
*   1 large egg
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   Pinch of black pepper

For the Filling:
*   1 cup mixed seafood (shrimp, squid rings, mussels, oysters, scallops – chopped into bite-sized pieces if large)
*   1 bunch green onions (about 10-12 stalks), cut into 3-4 inch lengths
*   1/2 yellow onion, thinly sliced
*   1/2 red bell pepper, thinly sliced (for color and sweetness, optional)
*   1-2 green chili peppers (like serrano or jalapeño), thinly sliced (for a spicy kick, optional)
*   Vegetable oil, for frying

For the Dipping Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons soy sauce
*   1 tablespoon rice vinegar
*   1 teaspoon sesame oil
*   1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds
*   1 clove garlic, minced
*   1 green onion, finely chopped
*   Pinch of red chili flakes (gochugaru, optional)

## How to Make Haemul Pajeon (Step-by-Step)

Making Haemul Pajeon is a straightforward process that yields incredibly delicious results. Follow these steps for a successful pancake:

1.  **Prepare the Seafood:** If using frozen seafood, thaw it completely and pat it dry with paper towels. Cut any larger pieces (like shrimp or squid) into bite-sized portions. This ensures even cooking and easier eating.
2.  **Make the Batter:** In a large bowl, whisk together the Korean pancake mix (or flours), cold water (or broth), egg, salt, and black pepper until just combined. Don't overmix; a few lumps are fine. The batter should be slightly thicker than crêpe batter, able to coat the back of a spoon. If it's too thick, add a tablespoon of water at a time until the desired consistency is reached.
3.  **Prepare Vegetables:** Wash and trim the green onions, cutting them into 3-4 inch segments. Thinly slice the yellow onion, red bell pepper, and green chilies (if using).
4.  **Combine Ingredients (Optional Method 1):** You can mix all the seafood and vegetables directly into the batter. This is the simplest method, ensuring everything is evenly coated.
5.  **Prepare for Frying (Method 2 - Layering):** This method often produces a prettier pancake with more distinct layers of ingredients. Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil, ensuring the entire surface is coated.
6.  **Arrange Ingredients and Pour Batter (Method 2):** Once the oil is hot (it should shimmer), arrange a layer of green onions in the pan, ensuring they cover the surface. Scatter some of the prepared seafood, sliced yellow onions, and bell peppers over the green onions. Carefully pour about 1/2 to 3/4 cup of batter over the arranged ingredients, spreading it gently to cover everything and fill any gaps.
7.  **Cook the First Side:** Let the pancake cook undisturbed for 4-6 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and crispy, and the top is mostly set.
8.  **Flip the Pancake:** Drizzle a little more oil around the edges of the pancake. Using a large spatula (or two, if needed), carefully flip the Haemul Pajeon. Press down gently with the spatula to ensure good contact with the pan.
9.  **Cook the Second Side:** Cook for another 3-5 minutes, or until this side is also golden brown and crispy, and the seafood is cooked through.
10. **Serve:** Slide the cooked Haemul Pajeon onto a cutting board. Cut it into wedges or squares and serve immediately with the dipping sauce. Repeat with remaining batter and ingredients.

## Tips for the Perfect Crispy Haemul Pajeon

Achieving that irresistible crispiness is key to a truly great Haemul Pajeon. Here are some expert tips:

*   **Cold Water/Broth:** Using very cold water or broth for the batter helps create a lighter, crispier texture. The cold liquid inhibits gluten development and results in a more delicate crust.
*   **Don't Overmix the Batter:** Overmixing develops gluten, leading to a chewier, tougher pancake. Mix just until the ingredients are combined.
*   **Hot Pan, Plenty of Oil:** A screaming hot pan and a generous amount of oil are crucial for a crispy exterior. Don't be shy with the oil – it helps fry the pancake rather than just cooking it. The oil should shimmer before you add the batter.
*   **Even Thickness:** Try to spread the batter and ingredients evenly in the pan. Thicker sections will cook slower and might not get as crispy.
*   **Resist Flipping Too Soon:** Patience is a virtue here. Let the first side cook thoroughly until it’s deeply golden and easily releases from the pan before attempting to flip. Flipping too early can cause the pancake to tear.
*   **Press Gently:** After flipping, gently press down on the pancake with your spatula. This ensures maximum contact with the hot pan, promoting even browning and crispiness.
*   **Single Layer of Ingredients:** While tempting to load up on seafood and vegetables, try not to overcrowd the pancake. Too many ingredients can make it difficult for the batter to crisp up properly.

## Serving Suggestions & Dipping Sauce

Haemul Pajeon is best enjoyed fresh off the pan, while it's still warm and crispy. It’s a fantastic appetizer, a hearty snack, or even a light meal.

**Dipping Sauce:** The simple yet flavorful dipping sauce is essential for complementing the richness of the pancake. To make it, combine 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 1 tablespoon rice vinegar, 1 teaspoon sesame oil, 1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds, 1 minced garlic clove, 1 finely chopped green onion, and a pinch of red chili flakes (gochugaru) if you like a little heat. Stir well and serve alongside your Haemul Pajeon.

**Pairings:**
*   **Makgeolli:** As mentioned, Korean rice wine is the traditional accompaniment, especially on a rainy day.
*   **Kimchi:** A side of fresh or fermented kimchi always pairs wonderfully with savory Korean dishes.
*   **Pickled Radish (Danmuji):** The tangy crunch of pickled radish offers a refreshing contrast.
*   **Other Banchan:** Feel free to serve it with other small Korean side dishes you enjoy.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Haemul Pajeon is a masterpiece, there are many ways to customize it to your taste or what you have on hand:

*   **Vegetable Pajeon (Yachaejeon):** If seafood isn't your preference, you can make a purely vegetable version. Load it up with sliced carrots, zucchini, mushrooms, bell peppers, and onions.
*   **Kimchi Pajeon (Kimchijeon):** This popular variation incorporates chopped fermented kimchi into the batter, giving the pancake a spicy, tangy kick. Often, a little pork belly or tuna is added with the kimchi.
*   **Meat Pajeon (Gogi Pajeon):** Thinly sliced beef (like bulgogi meat) or pork can be used instead of or in addition to seafood for a richer, meatier pancake.
*   **Flour Substitutions:** While Korean pancake mix is ideal, a blend of all-purpose flour and rice flour (about 2:1 ratio) works well. The rice flour contributes to the crispiness.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of green chilies or add a pinch of gochugaru (Korean chili powder) to the batter for more heat.
*   **Herb Additions:** Fresh perilla leaves (kkaennip) or chives can be added for extra aroma and flavor.

Haemul Pajeon is more than just a pancake; it's a celebration of fresh ingredients, satisfying textures, and comforting flavors. With this guide, you're well-equipped to recreate this beloved Korean dish in your own kitchen. Don't be afraid to experiment with the seafood and vegetables, and most importantly, enjoy the process of making and savoring your very own crispy, savory Haemul Pajeon.
